chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

I said to him: Is the testimony of women permissible in marriage or divorce or in stoning? He said: 'The testimony of women is permissible in what men cannot see, and there is no man with them; and their testimony is permissible in marriage if there is a man with them; and their testimony is permissible in the punishment of adultery if there are three men and two women; and the testimony of two men and four women is not permissible in adultery and stoning; and their testimony is not permissible in divorce nor in blood (diyah).'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for women's testimony in marriage, divorce, and adultery according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarates the jurisprudential nuances of women's testimony (shahadat al-nisa) within the Shia school, distinguishing between contexts where their testimony stands alone versus those requiring male witnesses. It specifically mandates that for hudud of zina and rجم, the ratio is three men and two women, while explicitly excluding women from testifying in cases of talaq (divorce) and damm (blood money). This ruling reflects the practical application of Quranic principles regarding witness reliability in matters where men are typically the primary observers.
